target_customer: Minecraft players and friend groups who want a hosted multiplayer server without managing hardware
problem: Running a Minecraft server cost around 70 dollars a month for self-hosting and required hardware skill; Minefold offered per-player accounts so cost is shared, for about 5 dollars a month.
business_model: Consumer subscription and hourly or plan-based game server hosting

founders.name: Chris Lloyd
founders.background_notes: Sydney, Australia, relocated for YC per TechCrunch 2012-03-12.

founders.name: Dave Newman
founders.background_notes: YC page says later cofounder and CTO of howie.com. Listed as David Newman by TechCrunch.

technical_complexity.rationale: On-demand server provisioning in under 30 seconds with a Heroku-inspired architecture, plus map rendering, is solid engineering for two people.

defensibility.rationale: Hosting Minecraft servers was copyable and dependent on Mojang's game; the official hosted offering later appeared.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not confirmed for Minefold. Search results mention Mojang's later Realms service as a hosted alternative but give no date.

market_need_then: Minecraft was growing quickly in 2011 and 2012; TechCrunch reported over 6,000 hours played through Minefold since a December 2011 soft launch.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Kotaku in 2011-10 and TechCrunch in 2012-03.

brand_strength.rationale: The name nods to Minecraft but ties the brand to a third party game; press coverage was modest.

outcome_analysis: Minefold was a two-founder Winter 2012 YC company hosting Minecraft servers on demand, which soft-launched in December 2011. YC lists it inactive but no shutdown notice, acquisition or reason was found, and no funding beyond the YC participation. The cause of its end is not public, so failure factors are empty.
notes: minefold.com returned HTTP 503 so the site may be dead. TechCrunch names no direct hosting competitors, only comparing to Amazon EC2 and Heroku; Kotaku names none. A search for rivals returned only modern hosting guides, so the competitor list is empty. Outcome and funding searches found nothing on Minefold. Founding year 2011 is inferred from the Kotaku October 2011 beta article.
